subject: Clarify model-improvement exclusion and prompt/response custody for pilot
messages:
From: Lisa Foster <lisa.foster@pioneerhealth.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot contracting question — model improvement exclusion and prompt custody

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — PioneerHealth is excited to move the pilot forward. Legal asked me to confirm a couple of points before we sign the SOW:

1) We need an explicit commitment that PioneerHealth data will not be used to improve or re-train Redwood-hosted models (training/exposure exclusion). We understand the hosted product has variants — is there standard DPA language you can provide that states no-model-improvement for customer workloads?

2) Ownership/rights: we need assurance that prompts and generated responses we submit to the API are treated as our confidential data. Specifically: prompt and response custody, any right to export full transcripts, and whether Redwood keeps derivative artifacts.

Can you loop in legal/ops and send a redline or a short amendment we can share internally? If you have an evidence pack or runbook for how you operationalize a training block (logs, KV cache policies, subprocessor gating) that would be helpful for our compliance team.

Attachments: preliminary DPA excerpt (we added comments) — see attached.

Best,
Lisa Foster
Head of Product, PioneerHealth
From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Foster <lisa.foster@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contracting question — model improvement exclusion and prompt custody

Hi Lisa — thanks, and great running through the pilot scope yesterday. Looping in Kimberly (privacy/legal) and Marissa (ops) to propose concrete language and the operational checklist.

Short answers up front:
- We can commit to exclude PioneerHealth pilot traffic from any model improvement pipelines for the duration of the engagement (and optionally for an agreed retention window after).
- Prompts and generated responses will be marked as customer-owned interaction content; we support full transcript export on request and can include that in the DPA addendum.

Kimberly/Marissa: can you review the Pioneer-attached DPA excerpt and suggest a minimal amendment that covers:
- an explicit "model improvement exclusion" clause (scoped to pilot prod/endpoint IDs),
- a definition of "customer interaction data" (prompts, responses, metadata) and statement of customer ownership,
- operational evidence — what we provide (audit logs, snapshots, SFTP export) and expected delivery SLAs.

Lisa: we'll produce a redline + an operations appendix by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, Lisa Foster <lisa.foster@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contracting question — model improvement exclusion and prompt custody

Hi all — I reviewed PioneerHealth's excerpt and drafted a short addendum that handles both contract language and the operational proofs Pioneer asked for. Key points from our side:

Proposed contract language (summary):
- "Model Improvement Exclusion": Redwood will not use Customer Interaction Data to improve, update, or re-train any public or internal foundation models, model weights, or training pipelines; exclusion is scoped to the Project IDs specified in Schedule A and remains effective for the Term and a 90-day post-Term window unless otherwise agreed.
- "Customer Interaction Data Ownership": Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in prompts, responses, and associated customer metadata submitted to Redwood. Redwood obtains no derivative IP rights beyond providing inference services.
- "Evidence and Audit": Redwood will provide (i) daily request logs for the pilot endpoints (hashed tokens redacted), (ii) weekly KV-cache purge confirmations, and (iii) upon request, a one-time export of full interaction transcripts delivered via secure SFTP within 3 business days.

Operational notes for compliance pack (to attach):
- How we operationalize the exclusion: routing rules to tag pilot traffic, config toggle to opt-out of improvement pipelines, periodic cache eviction, and subprocessor gating so downstream observability processors do not persist raw interactions.
- Subprocessors: we will list any downstream analytics or storage providers; Pioneer can require us to put a subprocessor-specific exclusion in the DPA.

Attachments included: DPA-addendum-draft.pdf (contract redline), pilot-ops-checklist.md (step-by-step), sample-audit-log-stub.csv.

Marissa: can you confirm the SFTP export cadence and whether we can commit to the 3-business-day SLA for a one-time export? Also advise on how we record the KT/purge confirmations.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy — Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Foster <lisa.foster@pioneerhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, legal@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contracting question — model improvement exclusion and prompt custody

Thanks Kimberly — this is exactly the level of detail our legal/compliance team wanted. A few quick asks so we can move to signature:

- Can you replace the 90-day post-Term window with a configurable option (Customer can elect 0/90/365 days) and reflect that choice in Schedule A?
- For the SFTP export, confirm encryption (AES-256) and that exported transcripts will include system metadata but will exclude any administrator-level debug traces.
- Please provide a one-page plain-English runbook we can attach to our internal SOC review; if Marissa can drop that in the Ops checklist we can get the pilot greenlit.

If we get those three items updated in the addendum, PioneerHealth legal is prepared to sign and we can kick off the pilot next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Lisa Foster
Head of Product, PioneerHealth
P.S. Attached our redline with inline comments for Schedule A — thanks.
